blocks.arabic_text: وَاِذَا ضَرَبْتُمْ فِي الْاَرْضِ فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ اَنْ تَقْصُرُوْا مِنَ الصَّلٰوةِ اِنْ خِفْتُمْ اَنْ يَّفْتِنَكُمُ الَّذِيْنَ كَفَرُوْا اِنَّ الْكٰفِرِيْنَ كَانُوْا لَكُمْ عَدُوًّا مُّبِيْنًا
blocks.text: When you travel on earth, there is no sin on you should you shorten your salaah if you fear an attack from the Kuffaar. Indeed the Kuffaar are your open enemies.

The person then asked, "Should we also shorten the salaah when we are in safety and not in fear (while travelling)?" Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) replied, "There was certainly an excellent example for you in Rasulullaah ﷺ."[^1]

Hadhrat Zaid bin Aslam reports that he once saw Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) perform salaah with his buttons open. When he asked Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) about it, he replied, "I have seen Rasulullaah ﷺ doing this."[^2]
Hadhrat Mu'aawiya bin Qurra (RA) opens his buttons to Emulate Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Qurra (RA) says, "I went to Rasulullaah ﷺ in the company of a group from the Banu Muzayna tribe and we pledged our allegiance to him. Rasulullaah ﷺ's buttons were open and I put my hand into the collar of his upper garment and felt the seal of prophethood." Hadhrat Urwa bin Abdullaah bin Qushayr says, "Whether summer or winter, I always saw Mu'aawiya (the son of Hadhrat Qurra (RA)) and his son with their buttons open (emulating Rasulullaah ﷺ)."[^3]
Giving Due Regard to all Those Who have Some Relationship with Rasulullaah ﷺ, Whether they are His Companions, His Family, His Tribe or his Ummah
A Group of Sahabah (RA) Argue About their Relationship with Rasulullaah ﷺ and He Confirms What they Say

Hadhrat Ka'b bin Ujrah (RA) says, "We were all sitting before (the room of) Rasulullaah ﷺ in the Masjid. We were a group from the Ansaar and there was also a group from the Muhaajireen and another from the Banu Haashim. We then started disputing about which of us were closer and more beloved to Rasulullaah ﷺ. We said, 'It is us, the group of the Ansaar. We believed in Rasulullaah ﷺ, followed him, fought by his side and our army was always at the throats of the enemy. We are therefore closer and more beloved to Rasulullaah ﷺ.' Our Muhaajireen brothers then said, 'It is us who migrated with Allaah and Rasulullaah ﷺ, separating from our tribes, families and wealth.
